sbh2.7:2.1: What are the aggregates, and what is skill-in-aggregates?
sbh2.7:2.4: Form-aggregate, feeling-aggregate, [Conjectural: perception-aggregate,] formations-aggregate, and consciousness-aggregate.
sbh2.7:3.1: The form-aggregate: whatever form there is, all of it is the four great elements,
sbh2.7:3.2: and what is derived from the four great elements.
sbh2.7:3.3: Form is also past, future, or present; inward or outward; gross or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near.
sbh2.7:4.2: Feeling arisen in dependence on contact to be felt as pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant.
sbh2.7:4.5: and feeling born from ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact.
sbh2.7:5.5: and the perception 'there is nothing' — perception of the base of nothingness.
sbh2.7:5.8: and perception born from ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact.
sbh2.7:6.2: The six volition-bodies: volition born from eye-contact, and from ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact.
sbh2.7:6.4: the other mental factors are also formations.
sbh2.7:7.2: Whatever is mind, [Conjectural: mentality, and consciousness].
sbh2.7:7.4: eye-consciousness; ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness.
sbh2.7:7.5: And this feeling, perception, formations, and this consciousness —
sbh2.7:7.6: Past, future, present; inward or outward — and so on in detail, as before.
sbh2.7:8.2: One who knows these dharmas as taught — by their distinct nature,
sbh2.7:8.3: by their manifold nature, and who does not apprehend anything beyond that,
sbh2.7:8.4: nor conceptually constructs anything beyond that.
sbh2.7:8.5: This, in summary, is called skill-in-aggregates.
sbh2.7:9.1: What is the distinct nature of the aggregates? The form-aggregate is one thing; the feeling-aggregate is another; and so on,
sbh2.7:9.2: each distinct, up through the consciousness-aggregate. This is distinct nature.
sbh2.7:10.2: The form-aggregate has many kinds, and is manifold in nature.
sbh2.7:10.3: By the division into great elements and [Conjectural: derived form]; by past, future, present, and so on;
sbh2.7:10.5: this is called manifold nature for the form-aggregate.
sbh2.7:10.6: The same applies, mutatis mutandis, to the remaining aggregates.
sbh2.7:11.1: And how does he not apprehend or conceptually construct anything beyond that?
sbh2.7:11.3: only the thing — and does not, apart from the aggregates, apprehend a self
sbh2.7:11.4: permanent, steady, of unchanging nature; nor does he apprehend anything as ‘mine.’
sbh2.7:11.5: He does not conceptually construct anything beyond that.
sbh2.7:12.14: body-element, tangible-element, body-consciousness-element, [Lacuna] dharma-element, mind-consciousness-element — these are called the elements.
sbh2.7:13.1: Furthermore, [that] these eighteen dharmas arise from their own respective element, from their own respective seed,
sbh2.7:13.2: from their own respective lineage — are born, come forth, and manifest;
sbh2.7:13.3: when one knows, accepts, and considers this —
sbh2.7:13.5: When one knows the proceeding of the eighteen dharmas from their own respective element,
sbh2.7:13.6: this is precisely skill-in-cause-and-condition — this is what skill-in-elements amounts to.
sbh2.7:14.2: What is skill-in-sense-bases? It is said:
sbh2.7:14.12: tangible sense-base, mind sense-base, and dharma sense-base.
sbh2.7:15.2: The eye is predominant; forms are the object; for the arising of eye-consciousness with its associates.
sbh2.7:15.3: and the mind that has just ceased is the immediate-condition.
sbh2.7:15.6: and the mind that has just ceased is the immediate-condition,
sbh2.7:15.7: for the arising of ear-consciousness with its associates.
sbh2.7:15.8: And so on, up through: mind as the immediate [condition], the attention born from it as the predominant-condition, the dharma as object — for the arising of mind-consciousness with its associates.
sbh2.7:15.9: Thus by three conditions — immediate-condition, object-condition, and predominant-condition —
sbh2.7:15.10: the proceeding of the six consciousness-bodies happens,
sbh2.7:15.12: Skill in conditions with respect to the inward and outward sense-bases — this is called skill-in-sense-bases.
sbh2.7:16.1: What is dependent origination? What is skill-in-dependent-origination?
sbh2.7:16.3: Ignorance-conditioned formations; formations-conditioned consciousness; consciousness-conditioned name-and-form;
sbh2.7:16.4: [continuing in detail through the twelve links] until: thus is the arising of this whole great mass of suffering. This is called dependent origination.
sbh2.7:17.1: Further, [that] dharmas alone [Conjectural: nourish] dharmas, dharmas alone [Conjectural: suffuse] dharmas;
sbh2.7:17.2: formations alone bring forth dharmas — because of cause-arisenness, because of dependent-arisenness — not having been, they come into being.
sbh2.7:17.3: Having come into being, they pass away again.
sbh2.7:17.4: Therefore these formations are impermanent; and what is impermanent has the nature of birth, aging, disease, death, grief, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and distress.
sbh2.7:17.5: By their nature-of-aging up through their nature-of-distress,
sbh2.7:17.6: they are suffering. What is suffering — being not-self-determining, weak — is not-self.
sbh2.7:17.7: When by these aspects there is, with respect to dependently-arisen dharmas, knowing-of-impermanence, knowing-of-suffering, and knowing-of-not-self —
sbh2.7:18.1: Skill-in-the-possible-and-impossible is also to be understood as just dependent-origination.
sbh2.7:18.3: By skill-in-the-possible-and-impossible, he knows that causation is [Conjectural: not disparate] —
sbh2.7:18.4: that for wholesome and unwholesome actions there is a fruit-of-result; [Lacuna]
sbh2.7:18.5: and that for unwholesome actions the fruit is unwished.
sbh2.7:18.6: When the knowing is thus, this is called skill-in-the-possible-and-impossible.
sbh2.7:19.1: These five skill-domains, in summary, are skill-in-specific-characteristic,
sbh2.7:19.4: The remaining four declare skill-in-general-characteristic. This is called the skill-object.
